issues.where: d6 (Referral Note from Primary Care, released at start)
issues.problem: The referral note explicitly states 'Patient has expressed hesitation about anticoagulation due to a family history of intracranial hemorrhage on warfarin' — this discloses the reluctant/hidden fact f12 (brother's ICH on warfarin) and the critical psychosocial concern f24 before the learner ever asks. This should be removed from the artifact or replaced with a generic 'anticoagulation discussion requested' without revealing the family history reason.

issues.where: a12 result (STOP-BANG) and a13 result (home oximetry)
issues.problem: STOP-BANG is a self-report questionnaire that must be administered by asking the patient the component questions (snoring, witnessed apneas, etc.); handing back a finished score of 5/8 as an 'exam/test' result without the learner eliciting components (which match reluctant fact f15/f16) bypasses interview-based elicitation of hidden facts. Likewise a13 hands over overnight oximetry desaturation to 88% as if objectively measured/reviewed, but this is 'patient-reported' per the result text, meaning it is being disclosed as a record review though it is actually self-report that should normally emerge only through conversation. Both actions in effect hand over reluctant information (snoring/apnea awareness, nocturnal hypoxia) that otherwise requires rapport-building questions; fix by either making these true instrument reviews with a scored outcome sheet artifact or removing them as actions and leaving disclosure to the interview tier facts (f15, f16).
